security_audit.summary: The skill is documentation-only, with no executable source files in the package. Confirmed risks are elevated installation commands, cloning third-party code, API key handling in .env files, and pipeline command examples that can call external model services. Most other static hits are false positives from markdown fences, directory trees, CLI option text, and quality metric prose; no prompt injection attempt was found.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before sudo commands and provide package-manager alternatives for each platform.
Pin the Paper2All repository to a reviewed commit and document dependency review before running pip install or pipeline scripts.
Use .env.example placeholders, warn users never to commit .env, and recommend least-privilege API keys.

remediation.issue: Optional logo search uses external APIs and downloads assets
remediation.suggestion: Disclose network egress for logo discovery and keep the feature disabled unless the user enables it.

content.user_title: Transform Papers Into Web, Video, and Posters
content.value_statement: Researchers often need paper websites, posters, and video abstracts under deadline. This skill guides Paper2All workflows that turn LaTeX or PDF papers into research promotion assets.
actual_capabilities: Guides Paper2All installation, dependency setup, and API key configuration.
Plans interactive academic websites from LaTeX or PDF papers.
Creates conference poster workflows with dimensions, branding, QR codes, and print checks.
Creates presentation video workflows with slides, narration, subtitles, and optional talking-head output.
Supports batch processing plans and model selection for multiple papers.
Provides quality checks for content, design, accessibility, performance, and print readiness.
limitations: The skill does not include Paper2All pipeline source code.
LLM generation requires external API keys and may send paper content to model providers.
Talking-head video generation requires a high-memory NVIDIA GPU.
Generated claims, citations, layouts, and media require human review before publication.

use_cases.title: Prepare Conference Materials
use_cases.description: Create a coordinated website, poster, and presentation video for a paper submission or accepted talk.

use_cases.title: Publish Paper Homepages
use_cases.description: Turn a LaTeX or PDF paper into an explorable web page for a lab site or preprint page.

use_cases.title: Create Video Abstracts
use_cases.description: Generate a short narrated presentation that summarizes findings for journals, courses, or social media.

prompt_templates.title: Create A Paper Website
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert my paper into an interactive website. Review the input files, suggest the best setup, and list what I should verify before publishing.

prompt_templates.title: Generate A Conference Poster
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a conference poster plan for my paper. Use the required poster size, highlight key findings, and include a print review checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Build A Full Package
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a complete research promotion package with website, poster, and video. Recommend the processing order, model settings, and review steps.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Batch Conversion
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a batch workflow for multiple papers. Define folder organization, output naming, cost controls, and review gates for each generated asset.

output_examples.input: A LaTeX paper with figures, tables, and bibliography needs a public project page.
output: A website generation plan with input checks and output folders.
A review checklist for figures, links, mobile layout, and accessibility.
Deployment guidance for GitHub Pages, lab hosting, or a personal server.

output_examples.input: A researcher needs a 48 by 36 inch conference poster for a poster session.
output: A poster workflow with size, section priority, branding, and QR code guidance.
A print readiness checklist for resolution, fonts, colors, bleed, and test prints.

output_examples.input: A journal submission needs a short video abstract for general readers.
output: A video plan with slide count, narration style, duration, and subtitle review.
Quality checks for factual accuracy, audio clarity, timing, and final encoding.

best_practices: Start from clean LaTeX with complete figures, tables, and bibliography files.
Review every generated claim, citation, image, and narration before publication.
Ask for confirmation before running install commands, pipeline scripts, or external API features.
anti_patterns: Running sudo setup commands without checking the package source and platform requirements.
Publishing generated websites, posters, or videos without expert review.
Putting real API keys in shared prompts, documentation, screenshots, or repositories.

faq.question: What input formats does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports LaTeX source directories and high-quality PDFs. LaTeX gives the best structure and asset extraction.

faq.question: Does this skill include the Paper2All code?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance for using the external Paper2All repository and its documented workflows.

faq.question: Which outputs can it help create?
faq.answer: It can guide creation of academic websites, conference posters, presentation videos, and combined dissemination packages.

faq.question: Are API keys required?
faq.answer: Yes, LLM-backed generation requires API keys. Google keys are optional for automatic logo discovery.

faq.question: Can it handle multiple papers?
faq.answer: Yes. The documentation includes batch organization and multi-paper workflow guidance.

faq.question: Should outputs be reviewed before sharing?
faq.answer: Yes. Users should review factual accuracy, citations, visual quality, accessibility, and printing requirements.
